model.title: Simplification of certain requirements for spatial information infrastructure in the Union (INSPIRE) (Omnibus VIII on environmental legislation)

summary.lead: Official summary (Legislative Observatory, Decision by Parliament, 1st reading):

blocks.text: The European Parliament adopted by 515 votes to 108, with 35 abstentions, amendments to the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive 2007/2/EC as regards simplification of certain requirements for the establishment of the Infrastructure for Spatial Information in the Union.
The matter was referred to the committee responsible for interinstitutional negotiations.

The proposal aims to amend INSPIRE as part of the Environmental Omnibus (Omnibus VIII) simplification package, and as the legislative component of the GreenData4All initiative. The proposal would streamline the INSPIRE Directive by removing redundant technical requirements for network services and data sharing, deferring instead to the horizontal data legislative framework.

Parliament largely supports the objectives of simplification and alignment with horizontal data legislation. However, it believes that the Commission's approach in certain areas risks undermining important safeguards specific to environmental geographic data.
The main amendments adopted in plenary concern the following points:
Ensuring the availability, accessibility and usability of environmental information

Members consider that high-quality, reliable and comparable environmental data are an essential prerequisite for the design, implementation, monitoring and enforcement of Union environmental law and policies. Maintaining the availability, accessibility and usability of environmental information therefore remains essential to ensuring a high level of environmental protection across the Union.
Member States should ensure that:

- the provision of spatial data sets and spatial data services, including through application programming interfaces, is based on open, documented, vendor-neutral, and geospatial standards . These standards include relevant standards and specifications such as those of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), as well as the API standards of the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) and comparable open specifications;
- the technical solutions chosen do not impair the cross-border discoverability, accessibility, usability, and re-use of spatial data.
Network of services
Member States should:

- ensure that spatial data sets falling within the scope of this Directive are made available and accessible in accordance with Directive (EU) 2019/1024, including through appropriate technical arrangements enabling discovery and access for public tasks relevant for the environment, while supporting interoperability and comparability of spatial data across the Union;

- ensure that public authorities are given the technical possibility to link their spatial data sets to relevant services provided for under Union law on data governance and data sharing. This possibility should also be made available upon request to third parties whose spatial data sets comply with applicable requirements with regard to metadata and interoperability provided for under Union law on data governance and data sharing.
Data sharing

Member States should ensure that public authorities are able to access and exchange spatial data covered by this Directive that is necessary for the performance of public tasks that may have an impact on the environment. Provisions governing the re-use of public sector information are laid down in Directive (EU) 2019/1024 and other related Union legislation. Member States should, where necessary, adopt or maintain national measures to ensure effective access for the purposes of data sharing.

The European Parliament has adopted a set of changes to a proposed EU directive that would simplify the rules for the Infrastructure for Spatial Information in the Union, known as INSPIRE. The vote was 515 in favour, 108 against, with 35 abstentions. The changes were sent to the committee responsible for negotiations with the other EU institutions.

The proposal is part of a wider EU effort to simplify environmental rules and to support the GreenData4All initiative. It would remove some technical requirements for network services and data sharing from the INSPIRE Directive, relying instead on general EU data legislation.

Parliament broadly supports the goal of simplifying the rules and making them consistent with general data law. However, it is concerned that some of the Commission's approach could weaken protections that are specific to environmental geographic data.

Parliament's main amendments stress that good environmental data is essential for making, carrying out, monitoring and enforcing EU environmental laws. Member States would need to make sure that spatial datasets and services are provided using open, documented, vendor-neutral standards, including those of the International Organization for Standardization and the Open Geospatial Consortium, and that the technical choices made do not stop data from being found, accessed, used and reused across borders.

On the network of services, Member States would have to make relevant spatial datasets available and accessible under the EU open data directive, in a way that supports discovery, access and comparability across the EU. Public authorities would have to be able to link their datasets to relevant data-sharing services, and third parties whose datasets meet the required metadata and interoperability rules could request the same option.

On data sharing, Member States would have to ensure that public authorities can access and exchange the spatial data they need to carry out public tasks affecting the environment. Where necessary, countries would adopt or keep national measures to make this access effective.
